classification.habit: Small tree or shrub; medicinal drug is a plant gall
classification.distribution: Associated with the northwestern Himalayan region and neighbouring areas

identification.description: The crude drug Karkatashringi consists of characteristic horn-like galls formed on Pistacia integerrima, rather than an ordinary plant organ.
identification.whole_plant: Pistacia integerrima is a small tree or shrub; the medicinal galls are induced on the plant.
identification.root: Woody root system; not the traded medicinal part.
identification.leaf: Compound pinnate leaves with narrow leaflets, characteristic of Pistacia.
identification.fruit: Small drupe; not the principal crude drug.

classical_reference.shloka_reference_status: source-hub-added; exact verse/edition requires text-level verification
reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

major_constituents: Resinous/terpenoid constituents reported in Pistacia galls
phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Gall chemistry is influenced by host plant and gall formation; exact profiles require authenticated crude drug studies.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Karkatashringi is a traditional plant-gall drug. Its pharmacological literature is limited compared with standardized modern medicines and should be interpreted cautiously.
modern_information.safety_notes: Authenticate the characteristic gall and host plant; do not substitute unrelated plant galls.

exam_points: Horn-like gall is the key crude-drug character
mnemonics: Karkata + shringi = crab-horn: remember the horn-like gall.
student.quick_revision: Karkatashringi is the characteristic gall of Pistacia integerrima, used as a crude-drug gall rather than as ordinary bark or fruit.

teaching_points: Teach crude-drug identification of a plant gall and its host species.
discussion_points: Why gall material should not be confused with normal plant tissue
practical_points: Observe shape, surface, hardness and internal structure of authenticated gall material.

doctor.quick_reference: Karkatashringi — Pistacia integerrima gall; gall is the useful part listed here.
key_precautions: Authenticate the gall and host plant.
Verify dose and formulation from authoritative references.
